name: stri_match
title: Extract Regex Pattern Matches, Together with Capture Groups

origin.description: Extract a regular-expression match and its capture groups.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

arguments.name: regex
arguments.text: A regular expression. Passed to the corresponding stri_match_*_regex function.

arguments.name: mode
arguments.text: Which match to return: "first" (the default), "all", or "last". A unique prefix is accepted.

origin.details: mode selects stri_match_first_regex, stri_match_all_regex, or stri_match_last_regex. The default mode is first. Further arguments are forwarded. A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, yields a missing result, and an empty pattern warns. An empty string is searched. The inputs are recycled to the longer length. Column 0 is the whole match. A group that did not participate is cg_missing. A miss fills that pattern's own columns with cg_missing, and extra columns beyond that pattern stay NA. A missing string stays NA. Named groups label the columns when pattern is a single pattern. The first column name is empty. opts_regex holds only the settings that were supplied. Named arguments are merged into that dict and passed through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns and is ignored. case_insensitive, comments, dotall (also dot_all), literal, multiline (also multi_line), unix_lines, and uword are ICU flags. error_on_unknown_escapes rejects an unknown backslash. time_limit and stack_limit are applied only when they are positive.
origin.value: A character matrix for first and last, or a list of matrices for all.
origin.example:
result <- stri_match("ab12", regex = "([0-9]+)")
cat(paste0('stri_match("ab12", regex = "([0-9]+)") returns ', paste(result, collapse = ", "), '.\n'))
